BEHIND THE ATLAS

Real data.
Room to explore.

Each world is a modular Blender asset with subdivision and material layers, exported as glTF. Rocky bodies have subtle illustrative relief. Earth combines a 4K geographic map, water roughness, moving clouds, an atmosphere and night-side city lights.

Ellipses use NASA eccentricities, with the Sun at one focus. Kepler’s equation controls orbital motion. Period ratios are preserved; distances and planet sizes are compressed independently.

Starting positions and orbital orientations are illustrative, not a live ephemeris. Surface spin uses an independent, gentle visual clock: one turn every 2–6 minutes, even when orbital movement is paused or set to zero. These are illustrative spin speeds; the data panel still shows the real sidereal periods. Axial tilts include retrograde Venus and Uranus.

22 selected moons are included: Earth’s Moon, Phobos and Deimos, the four Galilean moons, seven major Saturnian moons, the five major Uranian moons, and Triton, Proteus and Nereid. This is not every known moon. Moon periods and eccentricities use JPL mean elements; orientations and starting phases are simplified. Default planetary motion is 0.25 days per second, 160 times slower than the original setting. Moon orbits advance 0.0009375 days per second at that setting. Pause freezes both orbital clocks. Moon surfaces turn illustratively every three minutes, independently of their orbital phase.

NASA Planetary Fact Sheet ↗

Planet, Sun, ring and lunar maps by Solar System Scope, based on NASA imagery, licensed under CC BY 4.0. Earth’s map is resized and derived roughness/cloud-alpha maps are added. Nineteen moons use spacecraft-based maps, including the lunar map above, JPL/Caltech/USGS Viking and Voyager mosaics, and Paul Schenk’s Cassini mosaic of Enceladus (LPI, CC BY 4.0). Source maps have uneven coverage and may contain filled gaps or aesthetic processing. Titan haze, Proteus and Nereid surfaces, microrelief and solar plasma effects are illustrative. Each moon provides its image-source link. Lighting is balanced for the compressed display scale, not photometrically calibrated.

REAL STRUCTURES · ENHANCED VISIBILITY

Between the worlds.

Belts, dust and gas are placed using NASA and planetary research sources. Distances are compressed. Particle sizes, number density, colour and opacity are illustrative, not a view the naked eye would see. The black background and slow motion are preserved.

Moon imagery: JPL/Caltech texture-map archive and Paul Schenk’s Cassini Enceladus mosaic. These are visualization textures, not products for scientific measurement.
